args.name: autocolorscale
args.docString: Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `marker.colorscale`. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed.

args.name: cauto
args.docString: Determines whether or not the color domain is computed with respect to the input data (here in `marker.color`) or the bounds set in `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Defaults to `false` when `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` are set by the user.

args.name: cmax
args.docString: Sets the upper bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color` and if set, `marker.cmin` must be set as well.

args.name: cmid
args.docString: Sets the mid-point of the color domain by scaling `marker.cmin` and/or `marker.cmax` to be equidistant to this point. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color`. Has no effect when `marker.cauto` is `false`.

args.name: cmin
args.docString: Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color` and if set, `marker.cmax` must be set as well.

args.name: color
args.docString: Sets the marker color. It accepts either a specific color or an array of numbers that are mapped to the colorscale relative to the max and min values of the array or relative to `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` if set.

args.name: coloraxis
args.docString: Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are *coloraxis*, *coloraxis2*, *coloraxis3*, etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis.

args.name: colorscale
args.docString: Sets the colorscale. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd.

args.name: cornerradius
args.docString: Sets the rounding of corners. May be an integer number of pixels, or a percentage of bar width (as a string ending in %). Defaults to `layout.barcornerradius`. In stack or relative barmode, the first trace to set cornerradius is used for the whole stack.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the bars.

args.name: pattern
args.docString: Sets the pattern within the marker.

args.name: reversescale
args.docString: Reverses the color mapping if true. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. If true, `marker.cmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `marker.cmax` will correspond to the first color.

args.docString: Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array.

args.name: dtick
args.docString: Sets the step in-between ticks on this axis. Use with `tick0`. Must be a positive number, or special strings available to *log* and *date* axes. If the axis `type` is *log*, then ticks are set every 10^(n*dtick) where n is the tick number. For example, to set a tick mark at 1, 10, 100, 1000, ... set dtick to 1. args.docString: Replacement text for specific tick or hover labels. For example using {US: 'USA', CA: 'Canada'} changes US to USA and CA to Canada. args.docString: If *all*, all exponents are shown besides their significands. If *first*, only the exponent of the first tick is shown. If *last*, only the exponent of the last tick is shown. If *none*, no exponents appear.

args.name: shape
args.docString: Sets the shape of the pattern fill. By default, no pattern is used for filling the area.

args.name: size
args.docString: Sets the size of unit squares of the pattern fill in pixels, which corresponds to the interval of repetition of the pattern.

args.name: solidity
args.docString: Sets the solidity of the pattern fill. Solidity is roughly the fraction of the area filled by the pattern. Solidity of 0 shows only the background color without pattern and solidty of 1 shows only the foreground color without pattern.

returns.name: Pattern

bgcolor.name: color
bgcolor.docString: When there is no colorscale sets the color of background pattern fill. Defaults to a `marker.color` background when `fillmode` is *overlay*. Otherwise, defaults to a transparent background.

fgcolor.name: color
fgcolor.docString: When there is no colorscale sets the color of foreground pattern fill. Defaults to a `marker.color` background when `fillmode` is *replace*. Otherwise, defaults to dark grey or white to increase contrast with the `bgcolor`.

fgopacity.name: number
fgopacity.docString: Sets the opacity of the foreground pattern fill. Defaults to a 0.5 when `fillmode` is *overlay*. Otherwise, defaults to 1.

fillmode.name: enumerated
fillmode.docString: Determines whether `marker.color` should be used as a default to `bgcolor` or a `fgcolor`.

solidity.name: number

args.name: family
args.docString: HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available.

args.name: lineposition
args.docString: Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an *under*, *over* or *through* as well as combinations e.g. *under+over*, etc.

args.name: shadow
args.docString: Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. *auto* places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options.

args.name: style
args.docString: Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family.

args.name: textcase
args.docString: Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized.

args.name: variant
args.docString: Sets the variant of the font.

args.name: weight
args.docString: Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font.

args.name: alignmentgroup
args.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same alignmentgroup. This controls whether bars compute their positional range dependently or independently.

args.name: base
args.docString: Sets where the bar base is drawn (in position axis units). In *stack* or *relative* barmode, traces that set *base* will be excluded and drawn in *overlay* mode instead.

args.name: cliponaxis
args.docString: Determines whether the text nodes are clipped about the subplot axes. To show the text nodes above axis lines and tick labels, make sure to set `xaxis.layer` and `yaxis.layer` to *below traces*.

args.name: constraintext
args.docString: Constrain the size of text inside or outside a bar to be no larger than the bar itself.

args.name: customdata
args.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

args.name: dx
args.docString: Sets the x coordinate step. See `x0` for more info.

args.name: dy
args.docString: Sets the y coordinate step. See `y0` for more info.

args.name: hoverinfo
args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

args.name: hovertemplate
args.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `value` and `label`. Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`.

args.name: hovertemplatefallback
args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

args.name: hovertext
args.docString: Sets hover text elements associated with each (x,y) pair. If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (x,y) coordinates. To be seen, trace `hoverinfo` must contain a *text* flag.

args.name: ids
args.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

args.name: insidetextanchor
args.docString: Determines if texts are kept at center or start/end points in `textposition` *inside* mode.

args.name: insidetextfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `text` lying inside the bar.

args.name: legend
args.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

args.name: legendgroup
args.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

args.name: legendrank
args.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

args.name: legendwidth
args.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

args.name: meta
args.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

args.name: name
args.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover.

args.name: offset
args.docString: Shifts the position where the bar is drawn (in position axis units). In *group* barmode, traces that set *offset* will be excluded and drawn in *overlay* mode instead.

args.name: offsetgroup
args.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same offsetgroup where bars of the same position coordinate will line up.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

args.name: orientation
args.docString: Sets the orientation of the bars. With *v* (*h*), the value of the each bar spans along the vertical (horizontal).

args.name: outsidetextfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `text` lying outside the bar.

args.name: selectedpoints
args.docString: Array containing integer indices of selected points. Has an effect only for traces that support selections. Note that an empty array means an empty selection where the `unselected` are turned on for all points, whereas, any other non-array values means no selection all where the `selected` and `unselected` styles have no effect.

args.name: showlegend
args.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

args.name: text
args.docString: Sets text elements associated with each (x,y) pair. If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (x,y) coordinates. If trace `hoverinfo` contains a *text* flag and *hovertext* is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels.

args.name: textangle
args.docString: Sets the angle of the tick labels with respect to the bar. For example, a `tickangle` of -90 draws the tick labels vertically. With *auto* the texts may automatically be rotated to fit with the maximum size in bars.

args.name: textfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `text`.

args.name: textposition
args.docString: Specifies the location of the `text`. *inside* positions `text` inside, next to the bar end (rotated and scaled if needed). *outside* positions `text` outside, next to the bar end (scaled if needed), unless there is another bar stacked on this one, then the text gets pushed inside. *auto* tries to position `text` inside the bar, but if the bar is too small and no bar is stacked on this one the text is moved outside. If *none*, no text appears.

args.name: texttemplate
args.docString: Template string used for rendering the information text that appears on points. Note that this will override `textinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}". Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. All attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `value` and `label`.

args.name: texttemplatefallback
args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

args.name: uid
args.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

args.name: uirevision
args.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. Trace changes are tracked by `uid`, which only falls back on trace index if no `uid` is provided. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves.

args.name: visible
args.docString: Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If *legendonly*, the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible).

args.name: width
args.docString: Sets the bar width (in position axis units).

args.name: x
args.docString: Sets the x coordinates.

args.name: x0
args.docString: Alternate to `x`. Builds a linear space of x coordinates. Use with `dx` where `x0` is the starting coordinate and `dx` the step.

args.name: xaxis
args.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's x coordinates and a 2D cartesian x axis. If *x* (the default value), the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis`. If *x2*, the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis2`, and so on.

args.name: xcalendar
args.docString: Sets the calendar system to use with `x` date data.

args.name: xhoverformat
args.docString: Sets the hover text formatting rule for `x` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: *%h* for half of the year as a decimal number as well as *%{n}f* for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, *2016-10-13 09:15:23.456* with tickformat *%H~%M~%S.%2f* would display *09~15~23.46*By default the values are formatted using `xaxis.hoverformat`.

args.name: xperiod
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the period positioning in milliseconds or *M<n>* on the x axis. Special values in the form of *M<n>* could be used to declare the number of months. In this case `n` must be a positive integer.

args.name: xperiod0
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the base for period positioning in milliseconds or date string on the x0 axis. When `x0period` is round number of weeks, the `x0period0` by default would be on a Sunday i.e. 2000-01-02, otherwise it would be at 2000-01-01.

args.name: xperiodalignment
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the alignment of data points on the x axis.

args.name: y
args.docString: Sets the y coordinates.

args.name: y0
args.docString: Alternate to `y`. Builds a linear space of y coordinates. Use with `dy` where `y0` is the starting coordinate and `dy` the step.

args.name: yaxis
args.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's y coordinates and a 2D cartesian y axis. If *y* (the default value), the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis`. If *y2*, the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis2`, and so on.

args.name: ycalendar
args.docString: Sets the calendar system to use with `y` date data.

args.name: yhoverformat
args.docString: Sets the hover text formatting rule for `y` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: *%h* for half of the year as a decimal number as well as *%{n}f* for fractional seconds with n digits. args.name: yperiod
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the period positioning in milliseconds or *M<n>* on the y axis. Special values in the form of *M<n>* could be used to declare the number of months. In this case `n` must be a positive integer.

args.name: yperiod0

args.name: yperiodalignment
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the alignment of data points on the y axis.

args.name: zorder
args.docString: Sets the layer on which this trace is displayed, relative to other SVG traces on the same subplot. SVG traces with higher `zorder` appear in front of those with lower `zorder`.

args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

args.name: hoveron
args.docString: Do the hover effects highlight individual boxes or sample points or both?

args.name: hovertemplate
args.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. args.name: hovertemplatefallback
args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

args.name: hovertext
args.docString: Same as `text`.

args.name: ids
args.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

args.name: jitter
args.docString: Sets the amount of jitter in the sample points drawn. If *0*, the sample points align along the distribution axis. If *1*, the sample points are drawn in a random jitter of width equal to the width of the box(es).

args.name: legend
args.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

args.name: legendgroup
args.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

args.name: legendrank
args.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

args.name: legendwidth
args.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

args.name: lowerfence
args.docString: Sets the lower fence values. There should be as many items as the number of boxes desired. This attribute has effect only under the q1/median/q3 signature. If `lowerfence` is not provided but a sample (in `y` or `x`) is set, we compute the lower as the last sample point below 1.5 times the IQR.

args.name: mean
args.docString: Sets the mean values. There should be as many items as the number of boxes desired. This attribute has effect only under the q1/median/q3 signature. If `mean` is not provided but a sample (in `y` or `x`) is set, we compute the mean for each box using the sample values.

args.name: median
args.docString: Sets the median values. There should be as many items as the number of boxes desired.

args.name: meta
args.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

args.name: notched
args.docString: Determines whether or not notches are drawn. Notches displays a confidence interval around the median. We compute the confidence interval as median +/- 1.57 * IQR / sqrt(N), where IQR is the interquartile range and N is the sample size. If two boxes' notches do not overlap there is 95% confidence their medians differ. See https://sites.google.com/site/davidsstatistics/home/notched-box-plots for more info. args.name: offsetgroup
args.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same offsetgroup where bars of the same position coordinate will line up.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

args.name: orientation
args.docString: Sets the orientation of the box(es). If *v* (*h*), the distribution is visualized along the vertical (horizontal).

args.docString: Sets the position of the sample points in relation to the box(es). If *0*, the sample points are places over the center of the box(es). Positive (negative) values correspond to positions to the right (left) for vertical boxes and above (below) for horizontal boxes

args.name: q1
args.docString: Sets the Quartile 1 values. There should be as many items as the number of boxes desired.

args.name: q3
args.docString: Sets the Quartile 3 values. There should be as many items as the number of boxes desired.

args.docString: Array containing integer indices of selected points. Has an effect only for traces that support selections. args.name: showlegend
args.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

args.name: showwhiskers
args.docString: Determines whether or not whiskers are visible. Defaults to true for `sizemode` *quartiles*, false for *sd*.

args.name: sizemode
args.docString: Sets the upper and lower bound for the boxes quartiles means box is drawn between Q1 and Q3 SD means the box is drawn between Mean +- Standard Deviation Argument sdmultiple (default 1) to scale the box size So it could be drawn 1-stddev, 3-stddev etc

args.name: hoverinfo
args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

args.name: hovertemplate
args.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `open`, `high`, `low` and `close`. Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`.

args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

args.name: legendgroup
args.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

args.name: legendrank
args.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

args.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

args.name: low
args.docString: Sets the low values.

args.name: meta
args.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. args.name: uid
args.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

args.name: uirevision
args.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. args.name: y

args.name: yaxis
args.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's y coordinates and a 2D cartesian y axis. If *y* (the default value), the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis`. If *y2*, the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis2`, and so on.

args.name: zorder
args.docString: Sets the layer on which this trace is displayed, relative to other SVG traces on the same subplot. SVG traces with higher `zorder` appear in front of those with lower `zorder`.

a.name: data_array
a.docString: An array containing values of the first parameter value

a0.name: number
a0.docString: Alternate to `a`. Builds a linear space of a coordinates. Use with `da` where `a0` is the starting coordinate and `da` the step.

b.name: data_array
b.docString: A two dimensional array of y coordinates at each carpet point.

b0.name: number
b0.docString: Alternate to `b`. Builds a linear space of a coordinates. Use with `db` where `b0` is the starting coordinate and `db` the step.

carpet.name: string
carpet.docString: An identifier for this carpet, so that `scattercarpet` and `contourcarpet` traces can specify a carpet plot on which they lie

cheaterslope.name: number
cheaterslope.docString: The shift applied to each successive row of data in creating a cheater plot. Only used if `x` is been omitted.

color.name: color
color.docString: Sets default for all colors associated with this axis all at once: line, font, tick, and grid colors. Grid color is lightened by blending this with the plot background Individual pieces can override this.

customdata.name: data_array
customdata.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

da.name: number
da.docString: Sets the a coordinate step. See `a0` for more info.

db.name: number
db.docString: Sets the b coordinate step. See `b0` for more info.

ids.name: data_array
ids.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

legend.name: subplotid
legend.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

legendrank.name: number

legendwidth.name: number
legendwidth.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

meta.name: any

Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

name.name: string
name.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover.

opacity.name: number
opacity.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

uid.name: string

uirevision.name: any

visible.name: enumerated
visible.docString: Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If *legendonly*, the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible).

x.docString: A two dimensional array of x coordinates at each carpet point. If omitted, the plot is a cheater plot and the xaxis is hidden by default.

args.docString: Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `colorscale`. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed.

args.name: coloraxis
args.docString: Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are *coloraxis*, *coloraxis2*, *coloraxis3*, etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis.

args.name: colorscale
args.docString: Sets the colorscale. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `zmin` and `zmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd.

args.name: customdata
args.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

args.name: featureidkey
args.docString: Sets the key in GeoJSON features which is used as id to match the items included in the `locations` array. Only has an effect when `geojson` is set. Support nested property, for example *properties.name*.

args.name: geo
args.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's geospatial coordinates and a geographic map. If *geo* (the default value), the geospatial coordinates refer to `layout.geo`. If *geo2*, the geospatial coordinates refer to `layout.geo2`, and so on.

args.name: geojson
args.docString: Sets optional GeoJSON data associated with this trace. If not given, the features on the base map are used. It can be set as a valid GeoJSON object or as a URL string. Note that we only accept GeoJSONs of type *FeatureCollection* or *Feature* with geometries of type *Polygon* or *MultiPolygon*.

args.name: hoverinfo
args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

args.name: hovertemplate
args.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variable `properties` Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. args.name: ids

args.name: legend
args.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

args.name: legendgroup
args.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

args.name: legendrank
args.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. args.name: legendwidth
args.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

args.name: locations

args.name: meta
args.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. autocolorscale.name: boolean

cauto.name: boolean

cmax.name: number
cmax.docString: Sets the upper bound of the color domain. Value should have the same units as u/v/w norm and if set, `cmin` must be set as well.

cmid.name: number
cmid.docString: Sets the mid-point of the color domain by scaling `cmin` and/or `cmax` to be equidistant to this point. Value should have the same units as u/v/w norm. Has no effect when `cauto` is `false`.

cmin.name: number
cmin.docString: Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Value should have the same units as u/v/w norm and if set, `cmax` must be set as well.

coloraxis.name: subplotid
coloraxis.docString: Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are *coloraxis*, *coloraxis2*, *coloraxis3*, etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis.

colorscale.name: colorscale
colorscale.docString: Sets the colorscale. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `cmin` and `cmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd.

customdata.name: data_array
customdata.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

hoverinfo.name: flaglist
hoverinfo.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

hovertemplate.name: string
hovertemplate.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variable `norm` Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. hovertext.name: string

ids.name: data_array

legend.name: subplotid

legendgroup.name: string
legendgroup.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

legendrank.name: number

The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

legendwidth.name: number
legendwidth.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

meta.name: any

Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. reversescale.docString: Reverses the color mapping if true. If true, `cmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `cmax` will correspond to the first color.

scene.name: subplotid
scene.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's 3D coordinate system and a 3D scene. If *scene* (the default value), the (x,y,z) coordinates refer to `layout.scene`. If *scene2*, the (x,y,z) coordinates refer to `layout.scene2`, and so on.

showlegend.name: boolean

showscale.name: boolean
showscale.docString: Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace.

sizemode.name: enumerated

This factor (computed internally) corresponds to the minimum "time" to travel across two successive x/y/z positions at the average velocity of those two successive positions. All cones in a given trace use the same factor. With `sizemode` set to *raw*, its default value is *1*. With `sizemode` set to *scaled*, `sizeref` is unitless, its default value is *0.5*. With `sizemode` set to *absolute*, `sizeref` has the same units as the u/v/w vector field, its the default value is half the sample's maximum vector norm.

text.name: string

uid.name: string

uirevision.name: any

So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves.

args.name: yhoverformat
args.docString: Sets the hover text formatting rule for `y` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: *%h* for half of the year as a decimal number as well as *%{n}f* for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, *2016-10-13 09:15:23.456* with tickformat *%H~%M~%S.%2f* would display *09~15~23.46*By default the values are formatted using `yaxis.hoverformat`.

args.name: yperiod
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the period positioning in milliseconds or *M<n>* on the y axis. Special values in the form of *M<n>* could be used to declare the number of months. In this case `n` must be a positive integer.

args.name: yperiod0
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the base for period positioning in milliseconds or date string on the y0 axis. When `y0period` is round number of weeks, the `y0period0` by default would be on a Sunday i.e. 2000-01-02, otherwise it would be at 2000-01-01.

args.name: yperiodalignment
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the alignment of data points on the y axis.

args.name: ytype
args.docString: If *array*, the heatmap's y coordinates are given by *y* (the default behavior when `y` is provided) If *scaled*, the heatmap's y coordinates are given by *y0* and *dy* (the default behavior when `y` is not provided)

args.name: z
args.docString: Sets the z data.

args.name: zauto
args.docString: Determines whether or not the color domain is computed with respect to the input data (here in `z`) or the bounds set in `zmin` and `zmax` Defaults to `false` when `zmin` and `zmax` are set by the user.

args.name: zhoverformat
args.docString: Sets the hover text formatting rule for `z` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format.By default the values are formatted using generic number format.

args.name: zmax
args.docString: Sets the upper bound of the color domain. Value should have the same units as in `z` and if set, `zmin` must be set as well.

args.name: zmid
args.docString: Sets the mid-point of the color domain by scaling `zmin` and/or `zmax` to be equidistant to this point. Value should have the same units as in `z`. Has no effect when `zauto` is `false`.

args.name: zmin
args.docString: Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Value should have the same units as in `z` and if set, `zmax` must be set as well.

args.name: zorder
args.docString: Sets the layer on which this trace is displayed, relative to other SVG traces on the same subplot. SVG traces with higher `zorder` appear in front of those with lower `zorder`.

autocolorscale.name: boolean
autocolorscale.docString: Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `colorscale`. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed.

autocontour.name: boolean
autocontour.docString: Determines whether or not the contour level attributes are picked by an algorithm. If *true*, the number of contour levels can be set in `ncontours`. If *false*, set the contour level attributes in `contours`.

coloraxis.name: subplotid
coloraxis.docString: Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are *coloraxis*, *coloraxis2*, *coloraxis3*, etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis.

colorscale.name: colorscale
colorscale.docString: Sets the colorscale. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `zmin` and `zmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd.

connectgaps.name: boolean
connectgaps.docString: Determines whether or not gaps (i.e. {nan} or missing values) in the `z` data are filled in. It is defaulted to true if `z` is a one dimensional array otherwise it is defaulted to false.

customdata.name: data_array
customdata.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

dx.name: number
dx.docString: Sets the x coordinate step. See `x0` for more info.

dy.name: number
dy.docString: Sets the y coordinate step. See `y0` for more info.

fillcolor.name: color
fillcolor.docString: Sets the fill color if `contours.type` is *constraint*. Defaults to a half-transparent variant of the line color, marker color, or marker line color, whichever is available.

hoverinfo.name: flaglist
hoverinfo.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

hoverongaps.name: boolean
hoverongaps.docString: Determines whether or not gaps (i.e. {nan} or missing values) in the `z` data have hover labels associated with them.

hovertemplate.name: string
hovertemplate.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available.  Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`.

hovertemplatefallback.name: any
hovertemplatefallback.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

hovertext.name: data_array
hovertext.docString: Same as `text`.

ids.name: data_array
ids.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

legend.name: subplotid

legendgroup.name: string
legendgroup.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

legendrank.name: number
legendrank.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

legendwidth.name: number
legendwidth.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

meta.name: any
meta.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

ncontours.name: integer

opacity.name: number

reversescale.name: boolean
reversescale.docString: Reverses the color mapping if true. If true, `zmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `zmax` will correspond to the first color.

showlegend.name: boolean
showlegend.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

showscale.name: boolean
showscale.docString: Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace.

text.name: data_array
text.docString: Sets the text elements associated with each z value.

texttemplate.name: string
texttemplate.docString: For this trace it only has an effect if `coloring` is set to *heatmap*. Template string used for rendering the information text that appears on points. Note that this will override `textinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}". Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. All attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `x`, `y`, `z` and `text`.

texttemplatefallback.name: any
texttemplatefallback.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

uid.name: string
uid.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

uirevision.name: any
uirevision.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves.

b0.name: any

showscale.name: boolean

text.name: data_array

uid.name: string

args.name: customdata

args.name: dx
args.docString: Sets the x coordinate step. See `x0` for more info.

args.name: dy
args.docString: Sets the y coordinate step. See `y0` for more info.

args.name: hoverinfo
args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

args.name: hovertemplate

args.name: hovertemplatefallback
args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

args.name: hovertext
args.docString: Sets hover text elements associated with each (x,y) pair. If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (x,y) coordinates. To be seen, trace `hoverinfo` must contain a *text* flag.

args.name: ids
args.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

args.name: insidetextanchor
args.docString: Determines if texts are kept at center or start/end points in `textposition` *inside* mode.

args.name: insidetextfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `text` lying inside the bar.

args.name: legend
args.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

args.name: legendgroup
args.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

args.name: legendrank
args.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

args.name: legendwidth
args.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

args.name: meta
args.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

args.name: name
args.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover.

args.name: offset
args.docString: Shifts the position where the bar is drawn (in position axis units). In *group* barmode, traces that set *offset* will be excluded and drawn in *overlay* mode instead.

args.name: offsetgroup
args.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same offsetgroup where bars of the same position coordinate will line up.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

args.name: orientation
args.docString: Sets the orientation of the funnels. With *v* (*h*), the value of the each bar spans along the vertical (horizontal). By default funnels are tend to be oriented horizontally; unless only *y* array is presented or orientation is set to *v*. Also regarding graphs including only 'horizontal' funnels, *autorange* on the *y-axis* are set to *reversed*.

args.name: outsidetextfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `text` lying outside the bar.

args.name: selectedpoints
args.docString: Array containing integer indices of selected points. Has an effect only for traces that support selections. Note that an empty array means an empty selection where the `unselected` are turned on for all points, whereas, any other non-array values means no selection all where the `selected` and `unselected` styles have no effect.

args.name: showlegend
args.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

args.name: text
args.docString: Sets text elements associated with each (x,y) pair. If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (x,y) coordinates. If trace `hoverinfo` contains a *text* flag and *hovertext* is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels.

args.name: textangle
args.docString: Sets the angle of the tick labels with respect to the bar. For example, a `tickangle` of -90 draws the tick labels vertically. With *auto* the texts may automatically be rotated to fit with the maximum size in bars.

args.name: textfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `text`.

args.name: textinfo
args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on the graph. In the case of having multiple funnels, percentages & totals are computed separately (per trace). Flags are rendered in a fixed order; use `texttemplate` if you need explicit control over the rendered string, including the order of fields and surrounding text.

args.name: texttemplatefallback
args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

args.name: uid
args.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

args.name: uirevision
args.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. args.name: width
args.docString: Sets the bar width (in position axis units).

args.name: x
args.docString: Sets the x coordinates.

args.name: x0
args.docString: Alternate to `x`. Builds a linear space of x coordinates. Use with `dx` where `x0` is the starting coordinate and `dx` the step.

args.name: xaxis
args.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's x coordinates and a 2D cartesian x axis. If *x* (the default value), the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis`. If *x2*, the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis2`, and so on.

args.name: xhoverformat
args.docString: Sets the hover text formatting rule for `x` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. args.name: xperiod
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the period positioning in milliseconds or *M<n>* on the x axis. Special values in the form of *M<n>* could be used to declare the number of months. In this case `n` must be a positive integer.

args.name: xperiod0
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the base for period positioning in milliseconds or date string on the x0 axis. When `x0period` is round number of weeks, the `x0period0` by default would be on a Sunday i.e. 2000-01-02, otherwise it would be at 2000-01-01.

args.name: xperiodalignment
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the alignment of data points on the x axis.

args.name: y

args.name: y0

args.name: baseratio

args.name: hoverinfo

args.name: hovertemplate

args.name: hovertemplatefallback
args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

args.name: hovertext
args.docString: Sets hover text elements associated with each sector. If a single string, the same string appears for all data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order of this trace's sectors. To be seen, trace `hoverinfo` must contain a *text* flag.

args.name: ids
args.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

args.name: insidetextfont

args.name: label0

args.name: labels
args.docString: Sets the sector labels. If `labels` entries are duplicated, we sum associated `values` or simply count occurrences if `values` is not provided. For other array attributes (including color) we use the first non-empty entry among all occurrences of the label.

args.name: legendgroup

args.name: legendrank

args.name: uirevision
args.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. args.name: xgap

args.name: xperiod0
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the base for period positioning in milliseconds or date string on the x0 axis. When `x0period` is round number of weeks, the `x0period0` by default would be on a Sunday i.e. 2000-01-02, otherwise it would be at 2000-01-01.

args.name: xperiodalignment
args.docString: Only relevant when the axis `type` is *date*. Sets the alignment of data points on the x axis.

args.name: xtype
args.docString: If *array*, the heatmap's x coordinates are given by *x* (the default behavior when `x` is provided). If *scaled*, the heatmap's x coordinates are given by *x0* and *dx* (the default behavior when `x` is not provided).

autocolorscale.name: boolean
autocolorscale.docString: Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `colorscale`. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed.

coloraxis.name: subplotid
coloraxis.docString: Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are *coloraxis*, *coloraxis2*, *coloraxis3*, etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis.

colorscale.name: colorscale
colorscale.docString: Sets the colorscale. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `zmin` and `zmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd.

connectgaps.name: boolean
connectgaps.docString: Determines whether or not gaps (i.e. {nan} or missing values) in the `z` data are filled in. It is defaulted to true if `z` is a one dimensional array and `zsmooth` is not false; otherwise it is defaulted to false.

customdata.name: data_array
customdata.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

dx.name: number
dx.docString: Sets the x coordinate step. See `x0` for more info.

dy.name: number
dy.docString: Sets the y coordinate step. See `y0` for more info.

hoverinfo.name: flaglist
hoverinfo.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

hoverongaps.name: boolean
hoverongaps.docString: Determines whether or not gaps (i.e. {nan} or missing values) in the `z` data have hover labels associated with them.

hovertemplate.name: string
hovertemplate.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available.  Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`.

hovertemplatefallback.name: any
hovertemplatefallback.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

hovertext.name: data_array
hovertext.docString: Same as `text`.

ids.name: data_array
ids.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

legend.name: subplotid
legend.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

legendgroup.name: string
legendgroup.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

legendrank.name: number
legendrank.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

legendwidth.name: number
legendwidth.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

meta.name: any
meta.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

opacity.name: number

reversescale.name: boolean
reversescale.docString: Reverses the color mapping if true. If true, `zmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `zmax` will correspond to the first color.

showlegend.name: boolean
showlegend.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

showscale.name: boolean

texttemplate.name: string

Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}". Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. All attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `x`, `y`, `z` and `text`.

uid.name: string
uid.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

uirevision.name: any
uirevision.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. Trace changes are tracked by `uid`, which only falls back on trace index if no `uid` is provided. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves.

visible.docString: Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If *legendonly*, the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible).

args.name: autobinx
args.docString: Obsolete: since v1.42 each bin attribute is auto-determined separately and `autobinx` is not needed. However, we accept `autobinx: true` or `false` and will update `xbins` accordingly before deleting `autobinx` from the trace.

args.docString: Set a group of histogram traces which will have compatible bin settings. Note that traces on the same subplot and with the same *orientation* under `barmode` *stack*, *relative* and *group* are forced into the same bingroup, Using `bingroup`, traces under `barmode` *overlay* and on different axes (of the same axis type) can have compatible bin settings. Note that histogram and histogram2d* trace can share the same `bingroup`

args.name: cliponaxis
args.docString: Determines whether the text nodes are clipped about the subplot axes. To show the text nodes above axis lines and tick labels, make sure to set `xaxis.layer` and `yaxis.layer` to *below traces*.

args.name: constraintext
args.docString: Constrain the size of text inside or outside a bar to be no larger than the bar itself.
