args.name: insidetextfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `textinfo` lying inside the sector.

args.name: labels
args.docString: Sets the labels of each of the sectors.

args.name: legend
args.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

args.name: legendrank
args.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

args.name: legendwidth
args.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

args.name: level
args.docString: Sets the level from which this trace hierarchy is rendered. Set `level` to `''` to start from the root node in the hierarchy. Must be an "id" if `ids` is filled in, otherwise plotly attempts to find a matching item in `labels`.

args.name: maxdepth
args.docString: Sets the number of rendered sectors from any given `level`. Set `maxdepth` to *-1* to render all the levels in the hierarchy.

args.name: meta
args.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

args.name: name
args.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

args.name: outsidetextfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `textinfo` lying outside the sector. This option refers to the root of the hierarchy presented on top left corner of a treemap graph. Please note that if a hierarchy has multiple root nodes, this option won't have any effect and `insidetextfont` would be used.

args.name: parents
args.docString: Sets the parent sectors for each of the sectors. Empty string items '' are understood to reference the root node in the hierarchy. If `ids` is filled, `parents` items are understood to be "ids" themselves. When `ids` is not set, plotly attempts to find matching items in `labels`, but beware they must be unique.

args.name: sort
args.docString: Determines whether or not the sectors are reordered from largest to smallest.

args.name: text
args.docString: Sets text elements associated with each sector. If trace `textinfo` contains a *text* flag, these elements will be seen on the chart. If trace `hoverinfo` contains a *text* flag and *hovertext* is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels.

args.name: textfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `textinfo`.

args.name: textinfo
args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on the graph. Flags are rendered in a fixed order; use `texttemplate` if you need explicit control over the rendered string, including the order of fields and surrounding text.

args.name: textposition
args.docString: Sets the positions of the `text` elements.

args.name: texttemplate
args.docString: Template string used for rendering the information text that appears on points. Note that this will override `textinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}". Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. All attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `currentPath`, `root`, `entry`, `percentRoot`, `percentEntry`, `percentParent`, `label` and `value`.

args.name: texttemplatefallback
args.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

args.name: uid
args.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

args.name: uirevision
args.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. Trace changes are tracked by `uid`, which only falls back on trace index if no `uid` is provided. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves.

args.name: values
args.docString: Sets the values associated with each of the sectors. Use with `branchvalues` to determine how the values are summed.

args.name: visible
args.docString: Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If *legendonly*, the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible).

branchvalues.name: enumerated
branchvalues.docString: Determines how the items in `values` are summed. When set to *total*, items in `values` are taken to be value of all its descendants. When set to *remainder*, items in `values` corresponding to the root and the branches sectors are taken to be the extra part not part of the sum of the values at their leaves.

count.name: flaglist
count.docString: Determines default for `values` when it is not provided, by inferring a 1 for each of the *leaves* and/or *branches*, otherwise 0.

customdata.name: data_array
customdata.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

hoverinfo.name: flaglist
hoverinfo.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. Flags are rendered in a fixed order; use `hovertemplate` if you need explicit control over the rendered string, including the order of fields and surrounding text.

hovertemplate.name: string
hovertemplate.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `currentPath`, `root`, `entry`, `percentRoot`, `percentEntry` and `percentParent`. Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`.

hovertemplatefallback.name: any
hovertemplatefallback.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

hovertext.name: string
hovertext.docString: Sets hover text elements associated with each sector. If a single string, the same string appears for all data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order of this trace's sectors. To be seen, trace `hoverinfo` must contain a *text* flag.

args.name: alignmentgroup
args.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same alignmentgroup. This controls whether bars compute their positional range dependently or independently.

args.name: bandwidth
args.docString: Sets the bandwidth used to compute the kernel density estimate. By default, the bandwidth is determined by Silverman's rule of thumb.

args.name: customdata
args.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

args.name: fillcolor
args.docString: Sets the fill color. Defaults to a half-transparent variant of the line color, marker color, or marker line color, whichever is available.

args.name: hoverinfo
args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

args.name: hoveron
args.docString: Do the hover effects highlight individual violins or sample points or the kernel density estimate or any combination of them?

args.docString: Same as `text`.

args.name: ids
args.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

args.name: jitter
args.docString: Sets the amount of jitter in the sample points drawn. If *0*, the sample points align along the distribution axis. If *1*, the sample points are drawn in a random jitter of width equal to the width of the violins.

args.name: legend
args.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

args.name: legendgroup
args.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

args.name: legendrank
args.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

args.name: name
args.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover. For violin traces, the name will also be used for the position coordinate, if `x` and `x0` (`y` and `y0` if horizontal) are missing and the position axis is categorical. Note that the trace name is also used as a default value for attribute `scalegroup` (please see its description for details).

args.name: offsetgroup
args.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same offsetgroup where bars of the same position coordinate will line up.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

args.name: orientation
args.docString: Sets the orientation of the violin(s). If *v* (*h*), the distribution is visualized along the vertical (horizontal).

args.name: pointpos
args.docString: Sets the position of the sample points in relation to the violins. If *0*, the sample points are places over the center of the violins. Positive (negative) values correspond to positions to the right (left) for vertical violins and above (below) for horizontal violins.

args.name: points
args.docString: If *outliers*, only the sample points lying outside the whiskers are shown If *suspectedoutliers*, the outlier points are shown and points either less than 4*Q1-3*Q3 or greater than 4*Q3-3*Q1 are highlighted (see `outliercolor`) If *all*, all sample points are shown If *false*, only the violins are shown with no sample points. Defaults to *suspectedoutliers* when `marker.outliercolor` or `marker.line.outliercolor` is set, otherwise defaults to *outliers*.

args.name: quartilemethod
args.docString: Sets the method used to compute the sample's Q1 and Q3 quartiles. The *linear* method uses the 25th percentile for Q1 and 75th percentile for Q3 as computed using method #10 (listed on http://jse.amstat.org/v14n3/langford.html). The *exclusive* method uses the median to divide the ordered dataset into two halves if the sample is odd, it does not include the median in either half - Q1 is then the median of the lower half and Q3 the median of the upper half. The *inclusive* method also uses the median to divide the ordered dataset into two halves but if the sample is odd, it includes the median in both halves - Q1 is then the median of the lower half and Q3 the median of the upper half.

args.name: scalegroup
args.docString: If there are multiple violins that should be sized according to some metric (see `scalemode`), link them by providing a non-empty group id here shared by every trace in the same group. If a violin's `width` is undefined, `scalegroup` will default to the trace's name. In this case, violins with the same names will be linked together

args.name: scalemode
args.docString: Sets the metric by which the width of each violin is determined. *width* means each violin has the same (max) width *count* means the violins are scaled by the number of sample points making up each violin.

args.name: selectedpoints
args.docString: Array containing integer indices of selected points. Has an effect only for traces that support selections. Note that an empty array means an empty selection where the `unselected` are turned on for all points, whereas, any other non-array values means no selection all where the `selected` and `unselected` styles have no effect.

args.name: showlegend
args.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

args.name: side
args.docString: Determines on which side of the position value the density function making up one half of a violin is plotted. Useful when comparing two violin traces under *overlay* mode, where one trace has `side` set to *positive* and the other to *negative*.

args.name: span
args.docString: Sets the span in data space for which the density function will be computed. Has an effect only when `spanmode` is set to *manual*.

args.name: spanmode
args.docString: Sets the method by which the span in data space where the density function will be computed. *soft* means the span goes from the sample's minimum value minus two bandwidths to the sample's maximum value plus two bandwidths. *hard* means the span goes from the sample's minimum to its maximum value. For custom span settings, use mode *manual* and fill in the `span` attribute.

args.name: text
args.docString: Sets the text elements associated with each sample value. If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (x,y) coordinates. To be seen, trace `hoverinfo` must contain a *text* flag.

args.name: uid
args.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

Trace changes are tracked by `uid`, which only falls back on trace index if no `uid` is provided. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves.

args.name: visible
args.docString: Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If *legendonly*, the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible).

args.name: width
args.docString: Sets the width of the violin in data coordinates. If *0* (default value) the width is automatically selected based on the positions of other violin traces in the same subplot.

args.name: x
args.docString: Sets the x sample data or coordinates. See overview for more info.

args.name: x0
args.docString: Sets the x coordinate for single-box traces or the starting coordinate for multi-box traces set using q1/median/q3. See overview for more info.

args.name: xaxis
args.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's x coordinates and a 2D cartesian x axis. If *x* (the default value), the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis`. If *x2*, the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis2`, and so on.

args.name: xhoverformat
args.docString: Sets the hover text formatting rule for `x` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: *%h* for half of the year as a decimal number as well as *%{n}f* for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, *2016-10-13 09:15:23.456* with tickformat *%H~%M~%S.%2f* would display *09~15~23.46*By default the values are formatted using `xaxis.hoverformat`.

args.name: y
args.docString: Sets the y sample data or coordinates. See overview for more info.

args.name: y0
args.docString: Sets the y coordinate for single-box traces or the starting coordinate for multi-box traces set using q1/median/q3. See overview for more info.

args.name: yaxis
args.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's y coordinates and a 2D cartesian y axis. If *y* (the default value), the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis`. If *y2*, the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis2`, and so on.

args.name: yhoverformat
args.docString: Sets the hover text formatting rule for `y` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: *%h* for half of the year as a decimal number as well as *%{n}f* for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, *2016-10-13 09:15:23.456* with tickformat *%H~%M~%S.%2f* would display *09~15~23.46*By default the values are formatted using `yaxis.hoverformat`.

args.name: zorder
args.docString: Sets the layer on which this trace is displayed, relative to other SVG traces on the same subplot. SVG traces with higher `zorder` appear in front of those with lower `zorder`.

alignmentgroup.name: string
alignmentgroup.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same alignmentgroup. This controls whether bars compute their positional range dependently or independently.

bandwidth.name: number
bandwidth.docString: Sets the bandwidth used to compute the kernel density estimate. By default, the bandwidth is determined by Silverman's rule of thumb.

customdata.name: data_array
customdata.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

fillcolor.name: color
fillcolor.docString: Sets the fill color. Defaults to a half-transparent variant of the line color, marker color, or marker line color, whichever is available.

hoverinfo.name: flaglist
hoverinfo.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

hoveron.name: flaglist
hoveron.docString: Do the hover effects highlight individual violins or sample points or the kernel density estimate or any combination of them?

hovertemplate.name: string
hovertemplate.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. hovertemplatefallback.name: any
hovertemplatefallback.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

hovertext.name: string
hovertext.docString: Same as `text`.

ids.name: data_array
ids.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

jitter.name: number
jitter.docString: Sets the amount of jitter in the sample points drawn. If *0*, the sample points align along the distribution axis. If *1*, the sample points are drawn in a random jitter of width equal to the width of the violins.

legend.name: subplotid
legend.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

legendgroup.name: string
legendgroup.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

legendrank.name: number
legendrank.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

legendwidth.name: number
legendwidth.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

meta.name: any
meta.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

name.name: string
name.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover. For violin traces, the name will also be used for the position coordinate, if `x` and `x0` (`y` and `y0` if horizontal) are missing and the position axis is categorical. Note that the trace name is also used as a default value for attribute `scalegroup` (please see its description for details).

offsetgroup.name: string
offsetgroup.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same offsetgroup where bars of the same position coordinate will line up.

opacity.name: number
opacity.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

orientation.name: enumerated
orientation.docString: Sets the orientation of the violin(s). If *v* (*h*), the distribution is visualized along the vertical (horizontal).

pointpos.name: number
pointpos.docString: Sets the position of the sample points in relation to the violins. If *0*, the sample points are places over the center of the violins. Positive (negative) values correspond to positions to the right (left) for vertical violins and above (below) for horizontal violins.

points.name: enumerated
points.docString: If *outliers*, only the sample points lying outside the whiskers are shown If *suspectedoutliers*, the outlier points are shown and points either less than 4*Q1-3*Q3 or greater than 4*Q3-3*Q1 are highlighted (see `outliercolor`) If *all*, all sample points are shown If *false*, only the violins are shown with no sample points. Defaults to *suspectedoutliers* when `marker.outliercolor` or `marker.line.outliercolor` is set, otherwise defaults to *outliers*.

quartilemethod.name: enumerated
quartilemethod.docString: Sets the method used to compute the sample's Q1 and Q3 quartiles. The *linear* method uses the 25th percentile for Q1 and 75th percentile for Q3 as computed using method #10 (listed on http://jse.amstat.org/v14n3/langford.html). The *exclusive* method uses the median to divide the ordered dataset into two halves if the sample is odd, it does not include the median in either half - Q1 is then the median of the lower half and Q3 the median of the upper half. The *inclusive* method also uses the median to divide the ordered dataset into two halves but if the sample is odd, it includes the median in both halves - Q1 is then the median of the lower half and Q3 the median of the upper half.

scalegroup.name: string
scalegroup.docString: If there are multiple violins that should be sized according to some metric (see `scalemode`), link them by providing a non-empty group id here shared by every trace in the same group. If a violin's `width` is undefined, `scalegroup` will default to the trace's name. In this case, violins with the same names will be linked together

scalemode.name: enumerated
scalemode.docString: Sets the metric by which the width of each violin is determined. *width* means each violin has the same (max) width *count* means the violins are scaled by the number of sample points making up each violin.

selectedpoints.name: any
selectedpoints.docString: Array containing integer indices of selected points. Has an effect only for traces that support selections. Note that an empty array means an empty selection where the `unselected` are turned on for all points, whereas, any other non-array values means no selection all where the `selected` and `unselected` styles have no effect.

showlegend.name: boolean
showlegend.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

side.name: enumerated
side.docString: Determines on which side of the position value the density function making up one half of a violin is plotted. Useful when comparing two violin traces under *overlay* mode, where one trace has `side` set to *positive* and the other to *negative*.

span.name: info_array
span.docString: Sets the span in data space for which the density function will be computed. Has an effect only when `spanmode` is set to *manual*.

spanmode.name: enumerated
spanmode.docString: Sets the method by which the span in data space where the density function will be computed. *soft* means the span goes from the sample's minimum value minus two bandwidths to the sample's maximum value plus two bandwidths. *hard* means the span goes from the sample's minimum to its maximum value. uid.name: string

So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves.

visible.name: enumerated
visible.docString: Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If *legendonly*, the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible).

width.name: number

x.name: data_array
x.docString: Sets the x sample data or coordinates. See overview for more info.

x0.name: any

For example, *2016-10-13 09:15:23.456* with tickformat *%H~%M~%S.%2f* would display *09~15~23.46*By default the values are formatted using `xaxis.hoverformat`.

y.name: data_array

y0.name: any

args.docString: Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `colorscale`. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed.

args.docString: Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Value should have the same units as `value` and if set, `cmax` must be set as well.

args.name: coloraxis

hoverinfo.docString: Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

hovertemplate.name: string
hovertemplate.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available.  Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`.

hovertemplatefallback.name: any
hovertemplatefallback.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

hovertext.name: string
hovertext.docString: Same as `text`.

ids.name: data_array
ids.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

isomax.name: number
isomax.docString: Sets the maximum boundary for iso-surface plot.

isomin.name: number
isomin.docString: Sets the minimum boundary for iso-surface plot.

legend.name: subplotid
legend.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

legendgroup.name: string
legendgroup.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

legendrank.name: number
legendrank.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

legendwidth.name: number
legendwidth.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

meta.name: any
meta.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

name.name: string
name.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover.

opacity.name: number
opacity.docString: Sets the opacity of the surface. Please note that in the case of using high `opacity` values for example a value greater than or equal to 0.5 on two surfaces (and 0.25 with four surfaces), an overlay of multiple transparent surfaces may not perfectly be sorted in depth by the webgl API. This behavior may be improved in the near future and is subject to change.

opacityscale.name: any
opacityscale.docString: Sets the opacityscale. The opacityscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an opacity value. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 1], [0.5, 0.2], [1, 1]]` means that higher/lower values would have higher opacity values and those in the middle would be more transparent Alternatively, `opacityscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: 'min', 'max', 'extremes' and 'uniform'. reversescale.name: boolean
reversescale.docString: Reverses the color mapping if true. If true, `cmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `cmax` will correspond to the first color.

scene.name: subplotid
scene.docString: Sets a reference between this trace's 3D coordinate system and a 3D scene. If *scene* (the default value), the (x,y,z) coordinates refer to `layout.scene`. If *scene2*, the (x,y,z) coordinates refer to `layout.scene2`, and so on.

showlegend.name: boolean
showlegend.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

showscale.name: boolean
showscale.docString: Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace.

text.name: string
text.docString: Sets the text elements associated with the vertices. If trace `hoverinfo` contains a *text* flag and *hovertext* is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels.

uid.name: string
uid.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

uirevision.name: any
uirevision.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. value.name: data_array
value.docString: Sets the 4th dimension (value) of the vertices.

valuehoverformat.name: string

visible.name: enumerated
visible.docString: Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If *legendonly*, the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible).

x.name: data_array
x.docString: Sets the X coordinates of the vertices on X axis.

xhoverformat.name: string
xhoverformat.docString: Sets the hover text formatting rule for `x` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. y.name: data_array
y.docString: Sets the Y coordinates of the vertices on Y axis.

yhoverformat.name: string

z.name: data_array
z.docString: Sets the Z coordinates of the vertices on Z axis.

zhoverformat.name: string

args.name: alignmentgroup
args.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same alignmentgroup. This controls whether bars compute their positional range dependently or independently.

args.name: base
args.docString: Sets where the bar base is drawn (in position axis units).

args.name: cliponaxis
args.docString: Determines whether the text nodes are clipped about the subplot axes. To show the text nodes above axis lines and tick labels, make sure to set `xaxis.layer` and `yaxis.layer` to *below traces*.

args.name: constraintext
args.docString: Constrain the size of text inside or outside a bar to be no larger than the bar itself.

args.name: customdata

args.docString: Sets the y coordinate step. See `y0` for more info.

args.docString: An array containing types of values. By default the values are considered as 'relative'. However; it is possible to use 'total' to compute the sums. Also 'absolute' could be applied to reset the computed total or to declare an initial value where needed.

args.docString: Shifts the position where the bar is drawn (in position axis units). In *group* barmode, traces that set *offset* will be excluded and drawn in *overlay* mode instead.

args.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same offsetgroup where bars of the same position coordinate will line up.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

args.name: orientation
args.docString: Sets the orientation of the bars. With *v* (*h*), the value of the each bar spans along the vertical (horizontal).

args.name: outsidetextfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `text` lying outside the bar.

args.docString: Array containing integer indices of selected points. Has an effect only for traces that support selections. args.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

If trace `hoverinfo` contains a *text* flag and *hovertext* is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels.

args.docString: Sets the angle of the tick labels with respect to the bar. For example, a `tickangle` of -90 draws the tick labels vertically. With *auto* the texts may automatically be rotated to fit with the maximum size in bars.

args.name: textfont
args.docString: Sets the font used for `text`.

args.name: textinfo
args.docString: Determines what trace information appears on the graph. In the case of having multiple waterfalls, totals are computed separately (per trace). Flags are rendered in a fixed order; use `texttemplate` if you need explicit control over the rendered string, including the order of fields and surrounding text.

If *none*, no text appears.

ids.docString: Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type.

insidetextanchor.name: enumerated
insidetextanchor.docString: Determines if texts are kept at center or start/end points in `textposition` *inside* mode.

legend.name: subplotid
legend.docString: Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are *legend*, *legend2*, *legend3*, etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc.

legendgroup.name: string
legendgroup.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

legendrank.name: number
legendrank.docString: Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with *reversed* `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

legendwidth.name: number
legendwidth.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

measure.name: data_array
measure.docString: An array containing types of values. By default the values are considered as 'relative'. However; it is possible to use 'total' to compute the sums. Also 'absolute' could be applied to reset the computed total or to declare an initial value where needed.

meta.name: any
meta.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

name.name: string
name.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover.

offset.name: number
offset.docString: Shifts the position where the bar is drawn (in position axis units). In *group* barmode, traces that set *offset* will be excluded and drawn in *overlay* mode instead.

offsetgroup.name: string
offsetgroup.docString: Set several traces linked to the same position axis or matching axes to the same offsetgroup where bars of the same position coordinate will line up.

opacity.name: number
opacity.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

orientation.name: enumerated
orientation.docString: Sets the orientation of the bars. With *v* (*h*), the value of the each bar spans along the vertical (horizontal).

selectedpoints.name: any
selectedpoints.docString: Array containing integer indices of selected points. Has an effect only for traces that support selections. Note that an empty array means an empty selection where the `unselected` are turned on for all points, whereas, any other non-array values means no selection all where the `selected` and `unselected` styles have no effect.

showlegend.name: boolean
showlegend.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

text.name: string
text.docString: Sets text elements associated with each (x,y) pair. If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (x,y) coordinates. If trace `hoverinfo` contains a *text* flag and *hovertext* is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels.

textinfo.name: flaglist

Flags are rendered in a fixed order; use `texttemplate` if you need explicit control over the rendered string, including the order of fields and surrounding text.

textposition.name: enumerated
textposition.docString: Specifies the location of the `text`. *inside* positions `text` inside, next to the bar end (rotated and scaled if needed). *outside* positions `text` outside, next to the bar end (scaled if needed), unless there is another bar stacked on this one, then the text gets pushed inside. *auto* tries to position `text` inside the bar, but if the bar is too small and no bar is stacked on this one the text is moved outside. If *none*, no text appears.

texttemplate.name: string

Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}". Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Finally, the template string has access to variables `initial`, `delta`, `final` and `label`.

texttemplatefallback.name: any
texttemplatefallback.docString: Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed.

uid.name: string
uid.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

uirevision.name: any

Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. width.name: number
width.docString: Sets the bar width (in position axis units).

x.name: data_array
x.docString: Sets the x coordinates.

For example, *2016-10-13 09:15:23.456* with tickformat *%H~%M~%S.%2f* would display *09~15~23.46*By default the values are formatted using `xaxis.hoverformat`.

xperiodalignment.name: enumerated

args.name: customdatasrc
args.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `customdata`.

args.docString: Sets the fill color. Defaults to a half-transparent variant of the line color, marker color, or marker line color, whichever is available.

When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Additionally, every attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available.  Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example "<extra>{fullData.name}</extra>". To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`.

args.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `lon`.

args.name: meta
args.docString: Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index.

args.name: metasrc
args.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `meta`.

args.name: name
args.docString: Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the trace.

args.name: radius
args.docString: Sets the radius of influence of one `lon` / `lat` point in pixels. Increasing the value makes the densitymapbox trace smoother, but less detailed.

args.name: radiussrc
args.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `radius`.

args.name: reversescale
args.docString: Reverses the color mapping if true. If true, `zmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `zmax` will correspond to the first color.

args.name: showlegend
args.docString: Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend.

args.name: showscale
args.docString: Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace.

args.name: subplot
args.docString: mapbox subplots and traces are deprecated! Please consider switching to `map` subplots and traces. Learn more at: https://plotly.com/python/maplibre-migration/ as well as https://plotly.com/javascript/maplibre-migration/ Sets a reference between this trace's data coordinates and a mapbox subplot. If *mapbox* (the default value), the data refer to `layout.mapbox`. If *mapbox2*, the data refer to `layout.mapbox2`, and so on.

args.name: text
args.docString: Sets text elements associated with each (lon,lat) pair If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (lon,lat) coordinates. If trace `hoverinfo` contains a *text* flag and *hovertext* is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels.

args.name: textsrc
args.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `text`.

args.name: uid
args.docString: Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions.

args.name: uirevision
args.docString: Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. args.docString: Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If *legendonly*, the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible).

args.name: z
args.docString: Sets the points' weight. For example, a value of 10 would be equivalent to having 10 points of weight 1 in the same spot

args.name: zauto

args.name: zmax
args.docString: Sets the upper bound of the color domain. Value should have the same units as in `z` and if set, `zmin` must be set as well.

args.name: zmid
args.docString: Sets the mid-point of the color domain by scaling `zmin` and/or `zmax` to be equidistant to this point. Value should have the same units as in `z`. Has no effect when `zauto` is `false`.

args.name: zmin
args.docString: Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Value should have the same units as in `z` and if set, `zmax` must be set as well.

args.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `z`.

autocolorscale.name: boolean

In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed.

below.name: string
below.docString: Determines if the densitymapbox trace will be inserted before the layer with the specified ID. By default, densitymapbox traces are placed below the first layer of type symbol If set to '', the layer will be inserted above every existing layer.

coloraxis.name: subplotid
coloraxis.docString: Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are *coloraxis*, *coloraxis2*, *coloraxis3*, etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis.

colorscale.name: colorscale
colorscale.docString: Sets the colorscale. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsv, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `zmin` and `zmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd.

customdata.name: data_array
customdata.docString: Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, *scatter* traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements

customdatasrc.name: string
customdatasrc.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `customdata`.

hoverinfo.name: flaglist
hoverinfo.docString: Determines which trace information appear on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired.

hoverinfosrc.name: string
hoverinfosrc.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `hoverinfo`.

hovertemplate.name: string
hovertemplate.docString: Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, *xother* will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after *(x|y)other* will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, every attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available.  Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example "<extra>{fullData.name}</extra>". To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`.

hovertemplatesrc.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `hovertemplate`.

hovertext.name: string
hovertext.docString: Sets hover text elements associated with each (lon,lat) pair If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (lon,lat) coordinates. To be seen, trace `hoverinfo` must contain a *text* flag.

hovertextsrc.name: string
hovertextsrc.docString: Sets the source reference on Chart Studio Cloud for `hovertext`.

legendgroup.name: string
legendgroup.docString: Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items.

legendrank.name: number

The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout.

legendwidth.docString: Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace.

args.name: autosize
args.docString: Determines whether or not a layout width or height that has been left undefined by the user is initialized on each relayout. Note that, regardless of this attribute, an undefined layout width or height is always initialized on the first call to plot.

args.name: autotypenumbers
args.docString: Using *strict* a numeric string in trace data is not converted to a number. Using *convert types* a numeric string in trace data may be treated as a number during automatic axis `type` detection. This is the default value; however it could be overridden for individual axes.

args.name: calendar
args.docString: Sets the default calendar system to use for interpreting and displaying dates throughout the plot.

args.name: clickanywhere
args.docString: If true, `plotly_click` events will fire for any click position within the plot area, not just over traces. When clicking where there is no trace data, the event will have an empty `points` array but will include `xvals` and `yvals` with click coordinates in data space, and `xPixel` and `yPixel` with click coordinates in pixels, relative to the top-left corner of the graph div.

args.name: clickmode
args.docString: Determines the mode of single click interactions. *event* is the default value and emits the `plotly_click` event. In addition this mode emits the `plotly_selected` event in drag modes *lasso* and *select*, but with no event data attached (kept for compatibility reasons). The *select* flag enables selecting single data points via click. This mode also supports persistent selections, meaning that pressing Shift while clicking, adds to / subtracts from an existing selection. *select* with `hovermode`: *x* can be confusing, consider explicitly setting `hovermode`: *closest* when using this feature. Selection events are sent accordingly as long as *event* flag is set as well. When the *event* flag is missing, `plotly_click` and `plotly_selected` events are not fired.

args.name: colorway
args.docString: Sets the default trace colors.

args.name: computed
args.docString: Placeholder for exporting automargin-impacting values namely `margin.t`, `margin.b`, `margin.l` and `margin.r` in *full-json* mode.

args.name: datarevision
args.docString: If provided, a changed value tells `Plotly.react` that one or more data arrays has changed. This way you can modify arrays in-place rather than making a complete new copy for an incremental change. If NOT provided, `Plotly.react` assumes that data arrays are being treated as immutable, thus any data array with a different identity from its predecessor contains new data.

args.name: dragmode
args.docString: Determines the mode of drag interactions. *select* and *lasso* apply only to scatter traces with markers or text. *orbit* and *turntable* apply only to 3D scenes.

args.name: editrevision
args.docString: Controls persistence of user-driven changes in `editable: true` configuration, other than trace names and axis titles. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`.

args.name: font
args.docString: Sets the global font. Note that fonts used in traces and other layout components inherit from the global font.

args.name: height
args.docString: Sets the plot's height (in px).

args.name: hoveranywhere
args.docString: If true, `plotly_hover` events will fire for any cursor position within the plot area, not just over traces. When the cursor is not over a trace, the event will have an empty `points` array but will include `xvals` and `yvals` with cursor coordinates in data space, and `xPixel` and `yPixel` with cursor coordinates in pixels, relative to the top-left corner of the graph div. A `plotly_unhover` event fires when the cursor leaves the plot area.

args.name: hoverdistance
args.docString: Sets the default distance (in pixels) to look for data to add hover labels (-1 means no cutoff, 0 means no looking for data). This is only a real distance for hovering on point-like objects, like scatter points. For area-like objects (bars, scatter fills, etc) hovering is on inside the area and off outside, but these objects will not supersede hover on point-like objects in case of conflict.

args.name: hovermode
args.docString: Determines the mode of hover interactions. If *closest*, a single hoverlabel will appear for the *closest* point within the `hoverdistance`. If *x* (or *y*), multiple hoverlabels will appear for multiple points at the *closest* x- (or y-) coordinate within the `hoverdistance`, with the caveat that no more than one hoverlabel will appear per trace. If *x unified* (or *y unified*), a single hoverlabel will appear multiple points at the closest x- (or y-) coordinate within the `hoverdistance` with the caveat that no more than one hoverlabel will appear per trace. In this mode, spikelines are enabled by default perpendicular to the specified axis. If false, hover interactions are disabled.

args.name: hoversort
args.docString: Determines the order of items shown in unified hover labels. If *trace*, items are sorted by trace index. If *value descending*, items are sorted by value from largest to smallest. If *value ascending*, items are sorted by value from smallest to largest. Only applies when `hovermode` is *x unified* or *y unified*.

args.name: hoversubplots
args.docString: Determines expansion of hover effects to other subplots If *single* just the axis pair of the primary point is included without overlaying subplots. If *overlaying* all subplots using the main axis and occupying the same space are included. If *axis*, also include stacked subplots using the same axis when `hovermode` is set to *x*, *x unified*, *y* or *y unified*.

args.name: meta
args.docString: Assigns extra meta information that can be used in various `text` attributes. Attributes such as the graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `trace.name` in legend items, `rangeselector`, `updatemenus` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. One can access `meta` fields using template strings: `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index of the `meta` item in question. `meta` can also be an object for example `{key: value}` which can be accessed %{meta[key]}.

args.name: minreducedheight
args.docString: Minimum height of the plot with margin.automargin applied (in px)

args.name: minreducedwidth
args.docString: Minimum width of the plot with margin.automargin applied (in px)

args.name: paper_bgcolor
args.docString: Sets the background color of the paper where the graph is drawn.

args.name: plot_bgcolor
args.docString: Sets the background color of the plotting area in-between x and y axes.

args.name: selectdirection
args.docString: When `dragmode` is set to *select*, this limits the selection of the drag to horizontal, vertical or diagonal. *h* only allows horizontal selection, *v* only vertical, *d* only diagonal and *any* sets no limit.

args.name: selectionrevision
args.docString: Controls persistence of user-driven changes in selected points from all traces.

args.name: separators
args.docString: Sets the decimal and thousand separators. For example, *. * puts a '.' before decimals and a space between thousands. In English locales, dflt is *.,* but other locales may alter this default.

args.name: showlegend
args.docString: Determines whether or not a legend is drawn. Default is `true` if there is a trace to show and any of these: a) Two or more traces would by default be shown in the legend. b) One pie trace is shown in the legend. c) One trace is explicitly given with `showlegend: true`.

args.name: spikedistance
args.docString: Sets the default distance (in pixels) to look for data to draw spikelines to (-1 means no cutoff, 0 means no looking for data). As with hoverdistance, distance does not apply to area-like objects. In addition, some objects can be hovered on but will not generate spikelines, such as scatter fills.

args.name: template
args.docString: Default attributes to be applied to the plot. Templates can be created from existing plots using `Plotly.makeTemplate`, or created manually. They should be objects with format: `{layout: layoutTemplate, data: {[type]: [traceTemplate, ...]}, ...}` `layoutTemplate` and `traceTemplate` are objects matching the attribute structure of `layout` and a data trace.  Trace templates are applied cyclically to traces of each type. Container arrays (eg `annotations`) have special handling: An object ending in `defaults` (eg `annotationdefaults`) is applied to each array item. But if an item has a `templateitemname` key we look in the template array for an item with matching `name` and apply that instead. If no matching `name` is found we mark the item invisible. Any named template item not referenced is appended to the end of the array, so you can use this for a watermark annotation or a logo image, for example. To omit one of these items on the plot, make an item with matching `templateitemname` and `visible: false`.

args.name: transition
args.docString: Sets transition options used during Plotly.react updates.

args.name: uirevision
args.docString: Used to allow user interactions with the plot to persist after `Plotly.react` calls that are unaware of these interactions. If `uirevision` is omitted, or if it is given and it changed from the previous `Plotly.react` call, the exact new figure is used. If `uirevision` is truthy and did NOT change, any attribute that has been affected by user interactions and did not receive a different value in the new figure will keep the interaction value. `layout.uirevision` attribute serves as the default for `uirevision` attributes in various sub-containers. For finer control you can set these sub-attributes directly. For example, if your app separately controls the data on the x and y axes you might set `xaxis.uirevision=*time*` and `yaxis.uirevision=*cost*`. Then if only the y data is changed, you can update `yaxis.uirevision=*quantity*` and the y axis range will reset but the x axis range will retain any user-driven zoom.

In this mode, spikelines are enabled by default perpendicular to the specified axis. If false, hover interactions are disabled.

hoversort.name: enumerated
hoversort.docString: Determines the order of items shown in unified hover labels. If *trace*, items are sorted by trace index. If *value descending*, items are sorted by value from largest to smallest. If *value ascending*, items are sorted by value from smallest to largest. Only applies when `hovermode` is *x unified* or *y unified*.

hoversubplots.name: enumerated
hoversubplots.docString: Determines expansion of hover effects to other subplots If *single* just the axis pair of the primary point is included without overlaying subplots. If *overlaying* all subplots using the main axis and occupying the same space are included. If *axis*, also include stacked subplots using the same axis when `hovermode` is set to *x*, *x unified*, *y* or *y unified*.

meta.name: any
meta.docString: Assigns extra meta information that can be used in various `text` attributes. Attributes such as the graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `trace.name` in legend items, `rangeselector`, `updatemenus` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. One can access `meta` fields using template strings: `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index of the `meta` item in question. `meta` can also be an object for example `{key: value}` which can be accessed %{meta[key]}.

minreducedheight.name: number
minreducedheight.docString: Minimum height of the plot with margin.automargin applied (in px)

minreducedwidth.name: number
minreducedwidth.docString: Minimum width of the plot with margin.automargin applied (in px)

paper_bgcolor.name: color
paper_bgcolor.docString: Sets the background color of the paper where the graph is drawn.

plot_bgcolor.name: color
plot_bgcolor.docString: Sets the background color of the plotting area in-between x and y axes.

selectdirection.name: enumerated
selectdirection.docString: When `dragmode` is set to *select*, this limits the selection of the drag to horizontal, vertical or diagonal. *h* only allows horizontal selection, *v* only vertical, *d* only diagonal and *any* sets no limit.

selectionrevision.name: any
selectionrevision.docString: Controls persistence of user-driven changes in selected points from all traces.

separators.name: string
separators.docString: Sets the decimal and thousand separators. For example, *. * puts a '.' before decimals and a space between thousands. In English locales, dflt is *.,* but other locales may alter this default.

showlegend.name: boolean
showlegend.docString: Determines whether or not a legend is drawn. Default is `true` if there is a trace to show and any of these: a) Two or more traces would by default be shown in the legend. b) One pie trace is shown in the legend. c) One trace is explicitly given with `showlegend: true`.

spikedistance.name: integer
spikedistance.docString: Sets the default distance (in pixels) to look for data to draw spikelines to (-1 means no cutoff, 0 means no looking for data). As with hoverdistance, distance does not apply to area-like objects. In addition, some objects can be hovered on but will not generate spikelines, such as scatter fills.

uirevision.name: any
uirevision.docString: Used to allow user interactions with the plot to persist after `Plotly.react` calls that are unaware of these interactions. If `uirevision` is omitted, or if it is given and it changed from the previous `Plotly.react` call, the exact new figure is used. If `uirevision` is truthy and did NOT change, any attribute that has been affected by user interactions and did not receive a different value in the new figure will keep the interaction value. `layout.uirevision` attribute serves as the default for `uirevision` attributes in various sub-containers. For finer control you can set these sub-attributes directly. For example, if your app separately controls the data on the x and y axes you might set `xaxis.uirevision=*time*` and `yaxis.uirevision=*cost*`. Then if only the y data is changed, you can update `yaxis.uirevision=*quantity*` and the y axis range will reset but the x axis range will retain any user-driven zoom.

width.name: number
width.docString: Sets the plot's width (in px).

args.name: align
args.docString: Sets the horizontal alignment of the text content within hover label box. Has an effect only if the hover label text spans more two or more lines

args.name: bgcolor
args.docString: Sets the background color of the hover labels for this trace

args.name: bordercolor
args.docString: Sets the border color of the hover labels for this trace.

args.name: namelength
args.docString: Sets the default length (in number of characters) of the trace name in the hover labels for all traces. -1 shows the whole name regardless of length. 0-3 shows the first 0-3 characters, and an integer >3 will show the whole name if it is less than that many characters, but if it is longer, will truncate to `namelength - 3` characters and add an ellipsis.

args.name: showarrow
args.docString: Sets whether or not to show the hover label arrow/triangle pointing to the data point.

text.name: string

args.name: autocolorscale
args.docString: Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `marker.colorscale`. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed.

args.name: cauto
args.docString: Determines whether or not the color domain is computed with respect to the input data (here in `marker.color`) or the bounds set in `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Defaults to `false` when `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` are set by the user.

args.name: cmax
args.docString: Sets the upper bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color` and if set, `marker.cmin` must be set as well.

args.name: cmid
args.docString: Sets the mid-point of the color domain by scaling `marker.cmin` and/or `marker.cmax` to be equidistant to this point. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color`. Has no effect when `marker.cauto` is `false`.

args.name: cmin
args.docString: Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color` and if set, `marker.cmax` must be set as well.

args.name: color
args.docString: Sets the marker color. It accepts either a specific color or an array of numbers that are mapped to the colorscale relative to the max and min values of the array or relative to `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` if set.

args.name: coloraxis
args.docString: Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are *coloraxis*, *coloraxis2*, *coloraxis3*, etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis.

args.name: colorscale
args.docString: Sets the colorscale. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd.

args.name: opacity
args.docString: Sets the opacity of the bars.

args.name: pattern
args.docString: Sets the pattern within the marker.

args.name: reversescale
args.docString: Reverses the color mapping if true. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. If true, `marker.cmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `marker.cmax` will correspond to the first color.

args.name: showscale
args.docString: Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array.

In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed.

cmid.name: number

Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color`. Has no effect when `marker.cauto` is `false`.

cmin.name: number
cmin.docString: Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color` and if set, `marker.cmax` must be set as well.

color.name: color
color.docString: Sets the marker color. It accepts either a specific color or an array of numbers that are mapped to the colorscale relative to the max and min values of the array or relative to `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` if set.

coloraxis.name: subplotid
coloraxis.docString: Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are *coloraxis*, *coloraxis2*, *coloraxis3*, etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis.

opacity.docString: Sets the opacity of the bars.

showscale.name: boolean
showscale.docString: Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array.

args.name: family
args.docString: HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available.

args.name: lineposition
args.docString: Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an *under*, *over* or *through* as well as combinations e.g. *under+over*, etc.

args.name: shadow
args.docString: Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. *auto* places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options.

args.name: style
args.docString: Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family.

args.name: textcase

args.name: variant
